findings.quote: **Check 1.** A company enables the new AWS Security Hub. Will it show card numbers that Macie finds? ... No. Amazon Macie [is not automatically enabled]
findings.evidence: The premise says Macie already finds the card numbers, so Macie is running; the unified Security Hub correlates Macie signals (security-hub-renamed-cspm: 'Security Hub now automatically correlates security signals across ... sensitive data discovery (Amazon Macie)'), and Macie can publish findings to Security Hub CSPM (macie-eventbridge-and-security-hub). The cited fact security-hub-enables-cspm-not-macie only says enabling Security Hub does not turn Macie on. As written the answer teaches 'Security Hub does not show Macie findings', which is false. Fix: ask 'A company enables only the new AWS Security Hub. Does Macie start to look for card numbers?' (answer No, link stays), or keep the question and answer Yes, once Macie is enabled.

findings.quote: The delegated administrator exports for the organization, so one setting covers every member account.
findings.evidence: No fact in the canon says one export setting of the administrator covers all members, and the sentence has no fact link (RULINGS hard rule 1). GuardDuty administration is per Region: guardduty-delegated-admin-is-regional ('Unlike AWS Organizations, GuardDuty is a Regional service. The delegated GuardDuty administrator accounts and their member accounts must be added through AWS Organizations in each desired Region where you have GuardDuty enabled.'), so 'one setting' is misleading in a multi-Region organization. Fix in data/09-detection/questions.json (explanation of detection-q010): ground the key with guardduty-sra-export-findings-log-archive ('GuardDuty active findings are exported to a central S3 bucket in the Log Archive account, so you can retain the findings beyond 90 days') and say 'in each Region where GuardDuty runs' instead of 'one setting covers every member account'. The same edit applies to the 'Why not' of the Lambda option ('from the administrator account').
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Same fix as claims-07: guardduty-sra-export-findings-log-archive and guardduty-faq-regional-service ground the explanation; "one setting covers every member account" is gone.

findings.quote: detection-q005 (concept security-hub-single-view, status verified) is not shipped; no shipped question has AWS Security Hub as its answer
findings.evidence: The chapter's core teaching is the decision map, and 'a single view of security findings' is a signal row of 1-fast.md and the B-list of FREQUENCY.md (GuardDuty / Macie / Inspector / Detective / Security Hub / Config: '... aggregated findings ...'). Of the 10 shipped items, the correct answers are GuardDuty 4 times (q001, q009, q010, q011), Detective, Macie, Inspector, Artifact, Config history and Config-for-CSPM; Security Hub as aggregator is only a twin line (q008) and a distractor. q005 passed a unanimous three-lens solve. Ship q005 instead of q009, which repeats q001's GuardDuty concept at the same difficulty (2) and qualifier, so the difficulty mix does not change.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): The medium template ships exactly 5 core questions and q005 is core, q009 extended (Q201). Each core question is the only one for its service, or half of the required twin pair. q005 stays verified for drills and mocks, with its explanation fixed (technical-08).

findings.quote: detection-q007 (concept prevent-with-scp-detect-with-config, status verified, edited-pass) is not shipped; no shipped question tests a Config rule with automatic remediation or 'Config detects, SCP prevents'
findings.evidence: 2-deep.md teaches both as exam signal and trap ('"automatically remediate noncompliant resources" points to AWS Config remediation'; trap detection-trap-config-rule-prevents, facts config-faq-rules-evaluate-after-change-not-prevent and config-guide-remediation-ssm-automation), and FREQUENCY.md lists 'track config' / Config rules among the common keyword-to-service pairs, but no shipped item carries trap detection-trap-config-rule-prevents. Shipped multi-response share is 1 of 10 (SPEC.json questions.multi_share_of_bank 0.15). Ship q007 (difficulty 3, Select TWO) instead of q010 (difficulty 3), which keeps the difficulty mix and raises the multi share to 2 of 10.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): q007 set to ready (edited-pass), q010 set to verified. q lint 09 --ship: ok, multi 2, twin pairs 1.

findings.quote: The security team must receive an alert when an instance communicates with IP addresses that are known to be malicious. ... - Enable Amazon GuardDuty for every account in the organization through a delegated administrator, and review the results in the security account.
findings.evidence: The stem's requirement is an alert; every option ends with 'review the results in the security account', so the key does not literally deliver an alert and a careful reader can reject all four. Same wording in the twin detection-q006 ('must receive an alert when an instance runs a software package ...'). Fix both: either change the requirement to 'must see findings in the security account when ...', or end the key with 'and send the findings to an Amazon SNS topic with an Amazon EventBridge rule' (fact guardduty-findings-console-and-eventbridge / guardduty-automated-remediation-eventbridge-lambda) and give the distractors the same ending, so that the twins still differ by one phrase.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): A stem or option change alters what the blind solvers saw and needs a new verification round (R5); all three lenses agreed on the keys. Listed for the next question revision.

findings.quote: **Deciding question:** Is the auditor asking about the company's own resources, or about the AWS data centers and services?
findings.evidence: The table compares three services (Security Hub CSPM, AWS Config, AWS Artifact), but the deciding question only separates Artifact from the other two. Two of the three columns answer 'Yours', so a stem that asks 'CSPM or Config' is left undecided. The facts that decide it are in the canon: CSPM runs ready-made standards built on Config rules (security-hub-cspm-uses-config-rules, security-hub-cspm-standard-definition), while Config keeps configuration history and runs your own rules with remediation (config-faq-what-it-is, config-guide-remediation-ssm-automation). Add a second clause, for example: 'For your own resources: a ready-made security standard and one list of findings (CSPM), or your own rules, the history of a resource and remediation (Config)?'
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Deciding question now: "Reports about AWS (Artifact), a ready-made standard (Security Hub CSPM), or your own rules and history (Config)?"

findings.quote: | "known software vulnerabilities in EC2 instances" | Amazon Inspector | ... | traffic to a malicious IP address: Amazon GuardDuty |
findings.evidence: A 'but not if' guard should be a nearby stem phrase that flips the answer. A stem that mentions known vulnerabilities rarely also mentions malicious IP traffic, so this guard repeats the GuardDuty/Inspector trap instead of guarding the signal. The real flip on SAA stems is 'install the missing patches across the fleet' (Systems Manager Patch Manager: Inspector finds, it does not patch). Rule: TOOLS-rules/STYLE signals table, 'but not if' must name the phrase that changes the answer. Replace the guard with the patch case (link a verified Systems Manager fact from its home chapter, or mark it with an xref to the Systems Manager chapter).
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): But-not-if now: "patch the instances: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager" with an xref marker to chapter 38.

findings.quote: | An automatic response | An EventBridge rule |
findings.evidence: The automated response pattern (finding -> EventBridge -> Lambda or SNS) is the most common way a detection service appears in an SAA 'LEAST operational overhead' stem ('automatically notify' / 'automatically isolate'), and the canon holds it: guardduty-automated-remediation-eventbridge-lambda ('With GuardDuty, EventBridge, and AWS Lambda, you have the flexibility to set up automated remediation actions based on a security finding.'), macie-eventbridge-and-security-hub. The chapter gives it one unlinked table row, no exam signal and no question; no shipped option uses EventBridge as part of the key. Add a signal row or an Exam signal callout ('automatically respond to a GuardDuty finding'), link the fact in this row, and use it in a question (see exam-05 for one way to do this without a new item).
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Partial: the table row names an EventBridge rule and a Lambda function. A Go deeper was removed for the word budget (reader-15); a new question needs a verification round.

findings.quote: > **Changed recently:** (2025-12-02) Security Hub is now two services.
findings.evidence: RULINGS hard rule 7 requires a Changed recently note, with what older exam questions may assume, for each exam-relevant fact that changed since mid-2022; the section allows 3 entries and holds 1. Missing: (1) guardduty-malware-protection-s3-ga-2024-06 (June 11, 2024): older questions expect a self-built Lambda antivirus scan of S3 uploads, while detection-q011 now marks that option wrong; (2) detective-guardduty-requirement-removed (February 2, 2024; was 'GuardDuty enabled in your account for 48 hours'), exam_relevance core, today only a sentence in the 2-services.md card; (3) inspector-classic-full-shutdown-2026-05 (older questions about assessment templates and the Inspector agent). Add (1) and (2) as entries here; (3) can stay in the card.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Same as claims-15 for Detective. Fact guardduty-malware-protection-s3-ga-2024-06 has no changed record, and L107 needs the entry date to equal changed.date of the Now fact.

findings.quote: | [6 hours](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-eventbridge-subsequent-occurrences-default-6-hours) | Default event interval for repeated GuardDuty findings | Faster needs [15 minutes] |
findings.evidence: The A-list is for numbers that decide answers. The notification interval for subsequent occurrences of a finding does not decide a service choice in an SAA stem (new findings reach EventBridge in near real time: guardduty-eventbridge-new-findings-near-real-time), and putting it next to the 90-day retention numbers invites the belief that GuardDuty alerts are delayed by 6 hours. Move it to the B-list (and card detection-c006 to extended), or replace it with the near-real-time fact.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Partial: the row stays in the A-list because card c006 is a number card (C104 needs an A-list fact). The cell now says the interval is for repeats and that new findings arrive [near real-time].

findings.evidence: 3-do.md and 4-say.md print 'Nothing here yet.', and the task region of 1-fast.md 'Look first' is empty, because every item in data/09-detection/tasks.json (detection-t01, t02), speak.json (s01, s02) and cards.json is still status candidate, although the tasks, speak and cards stages are pass. TOOLS-items.md: 'Only items with status: ready are printed'; TOOLS-rules.md: 'A reviewer sets cards, speak items and tasks to ready in the stage of that kind, after the item lint is clean.' The two spoken prompts are the chapter's only practice in saying the decision map out loud, and the 'Try it' callout of 2-deep.md points to an empty file. Run set-status for the items after their item lint, then sync; the counts gate of finalize (T201, P201, C201) fails otherwise.

findings.quote: - Open the finding in AWS Security Hub CSPM, and create an insight that groups the related findings of the role.
findings.evidence: The option carries trap detection-trap-hub-or-detective-detects, whose belief is 'Turning on Security Hub or Detective gives threat detection by itself'. The misconception this option tests is different: 'a Security Hub insight explains the cause of one finding'. Either tag it with misconception text and no trap, or widen the trap's belief in brief.json to 'Security Hub detects threats or explains their cause'.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): Trap ids and beliefs belong to brief.json (orchestrator). The option still carries a belief close to the trap (Security Hub explains or detects by itself).

findings.quote: - Create a GuardDuty suppression rule for the finding type, and review the archived findings of the role.
findings.evidence: No candidate who wants the root cause of a finding would suppress it, so this option is eliminated without any knowledge and the item becomes a three-way choice. A more plausible fourth option: 'Enable VPC Flow Logs for the VPC, and analyze them with CloudWatch Logs Insights' (violates the qualifier and lacks API calls).
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): An option text change needs a new verification round (R5).

findings.quote: an auditor asks which inbound rules one specific security group had at a point in time three months ago.
findings.evidence: Three months is at the edge of the CloudTrail event history window, so a reader who knows that window may decide on that number rather than on 'what it looked like' versus 'who changed it', and CloudTrail events do carry the rule parameters. Use 'eight months ago' (Config keeps items for 7 years (2557 days) by default: config-retention-30-days-to-7-years) so the only deciding phrase is the point-in-time configuration.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): A stem change needs a new verification round (R5); all three lenses agreed on the key.

findings.quote: | Agent or log setup first? | No: it [pulls independent data streams directly] | ... |
findings.evidence: True for the foundational sources, but GuardDuty Runtime Monitoring needs an agent: guardduty-runtime-needs-security-agent ('Runtime Monitoring uses a GuardDuty security agent that adds visibility into runtime behavior, such as file access, process execution...'). A stem about process or file activity inside EC2 or containers points to GuardDuty with its agent. Add 'for foundational sources' to the cell, or a Go deeper line in 2-deep.md subsection 2.

findings.quote: and a daily schedule covers new transcripts without code.
findings.evidence: The schedule is the deciding requirement of the stem ('The check must run again every day'), and the canon holds it: macie-discovery-jobs-targeted ('run the job once on demand or on a recurring (daily, weekly or monthly) schedule'). Link it in the explanation so the reader learns the deciding fact.
findings.resolution: fix-09 (2026-10-13): q002 explanation now links [on a recurring basis for periodic analysis] (macie-discovery-jobs-targeted).

findings.quote: > **The exam probably expects:** no custom rules, only [your own threat lists](../facts/guardduty.md#guardduty-faq-no-custom-detections). Do not let this number decide an answer.
findings.evidence: 'this number' refers to nothing that decides an answer (the entry is a date), and the note sits under the B-list table. Say instead: 'Do not choose an option only because it writes custom GuardDuty detection rules.' The status line 'not examinable yet' is correct (fact guardduty-custom-detection-rules-2026-09, September 1, 2026, after the 2026-07-15 cut-off of RULINGS rule 7).
